the trunk must be straight or gently leaning, never wavy, of near-constant diameter

gaps.observation: The crown reads as a thin, short, straight-spoked starburst, not a rosette of long arching pinnate fronds with drooping lowest fronds.
Leaflets are minute ticks. The frond has no stiff, narrow leaflet volume and no bristly plumose silhouette.
The upper half of the trunk bends back and forth in a wavy S-shape, which violates the owner's straight-or-gently-leaning requirement.
The trunk shows sparse, isolated square knobs on a smooth shaft instead of a dense, tessellated spiral of leaf-base stubs.
There is no fibrous matting between trunk stubs.
There are no fruit clusters. The date cluster (fn-111) has not landed, and the fruitless crowns in reference-1 and reference-2 make fruit's core status uncertain.
The crown's foliage density and finish fall below the spruce anchor's catalogue floor.
There is no dead-frond skirt and no orange petiole sheath. These are secondary traits.

defects: rosette-crown-fronds (P-WHOLE, seed 1): the crown is a small, sparse starburst of thin, short, mostly straight spokes. It does not read as a rosette of long, arching pinnate fronds. In reference-0 and reference-1 the fronds are broad, feathery and strongly arching.
Fronds are far too thin and short. In the render, crown spread is roughly a quarter of trunk height. In reference-0, frond length is a large fraction of trunk length and the crown is broad and dense.
The lowest fronds dip only a little below the crown base. None hangs in a clear arch the way the drooping lower fronds do in reference-0 and reference-1.
The leaflets are tiny ticks along a hair-thin rachis. There is no visible stiff, narrow leaflet volume and no plumose or V-shaped frond section like the references show.
The upper trunk has a pronounced multi-bend S-wiggle. The owner explicitly requires the trunk to be straight or gently leaning, never wavy.
The trunk surface is a smooth shaft with sparse, isolated square knobs. It has no dense spiral diamond lattice of leaf-base stubs like reference-1 and reference-2.
The trunk has no fibrous matting between stubs. The render shows smooth, uniform bark.
Finish quality is below the spruce anchor floor. The anchor's foliage mass is dense and continuous, while the render's crown is a sparse, wiry sketch.

observations: The render shows one unbranched trunk with a mild basal flare, near-constant diameter and a slight taper. No branches or foliage grow from the trunk.
There are about 25–35 frond spokes. They radiate from a single apex in all directions, including some pointing below horizontal.
Frond colour is dark green, but it can barely be read at this scale.
There is no fruit, no dead-frond skirt and no petiole/sheath colouring. No crownshaft is visible, which is consistent with the references.

The reference-0 trunk curves and leans. The inventory treats this as variation, but the owner requirement that the trunk never be wavy takes precedence. The render's tight multi-bend wiggle differs from reference-0's single broad lean with a swollen base.
The spruce anchor was used for finish quality only, not for morphology.
